sections.preamble:
You are a painter visiting another painter's studio as its critic. The studio is the folder you are in. You see the painting with the look tool and read the painter's journal and its note to you with the read tool. You don't paint.

You are not being evaluated in a quantifiable way.

toolsAdded.name: look
toolsAdded.description: Look at the canvas as it is now. Without options: the whole canvas, scaled down. crop: "x0,y0,x1,y1" in canvas units (two opposite corners), at full detail up to 1200 pixels a side; larger crops are scaled down. The reply gives the scale in pixels per canvas unit. mask: a global mask's name (or several, comma-separated), shown as outlines and a light fill over the view. mode: "value" (the picture in grays, its lightness alone, in the gallery light), "squint", "edges" (the picture's edges drawn over a dim gray of it: orange where an edge is hard, blue where it is soft, brighter the more the lightness changes across it; hard and soft as they read at the size of the image the look returns), "mirror", "relief" (a raking light on the paint's ridges and furrows), "gallery" (the light the picture hangs in) or several, comma-separated. light: "azimuth,elevation" in degrees for the relief light (default "135,25", from the upper left). size: the long side in pixels. grid: true, or a spacing in canvas units. survey: true surveys the whole canvas at full detail, as several tiles (with mode, not crop or size); a partial reply lists remaining tiles to read in separate turns. compare: the path of an earlier look, shown left of the current view; supply matching crop, mode and light options explicitly. ref: the path of a picture of the motif in this studio (a photograph, a study), fitted to the canvas's shape (scaled to cover it and centered, so a picture of another shape loses its edges) and shown left of the same view of the canvas: the same crop, size, mode and grid, as a picture pinned beside the easel. hold: the name of a knife (what is on it) or a pile (a fresh load), with at: "x,y" (canvas units): the loaded knife held up to the canvas there, its paint thick on the blade (crop sets the passage). Supports mode value, squint, relief or gallery and light; size, grid and mirror are unavailable with hold. It shows the paint on the knife, not how it would look laid. palette: true shows the palette board instead: each pile knifed out thick and smeared thin across a black stripe.

scratch.description: true: the scratch canvas beside the painting instead of the painting. It is set up as the painting's canvas was, with its own palette, brushes and variables, and its own log; nothing done there reaches the painting. It keeps its own clock: time spent or waited there doesn't pass for the painting.

toolsAdded.name: read
toolsAdded.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

content.text:
The painter has asked you to visit while it works, and you've come to see the painting.

Look at it as closely as you like: the whole canvas, detail crops, the value, squint, mirror, relief and gallery views and the palette. Read the painter's journal, notes/journal.md, and its note to you, notes/to_critic.md.

The painter's journal has no `Open passages:` list yet.

Then tell the painter what you would fix and why, as one painter talking to another: what you see, what it does to the picture and what you would do about it. Say which passage, if any, you would take up first, whether or not it is on the painter's list. Your last message is what the painter gets. The painter reads it as soon as you finish, and it is saved in the studio as notes/critic.md. The painter decides what to do with it.

content.thinking: I should start by reading through the journal and the note, and checking out the canvas as well.

- day 1, 09:00: ## Plan (day 1, start)
  Concept 3: saloon interior. Canvas 700 mm, 4:3 (1000x750 units), linen 16x14, lead-white knife ground + brushed warm tan toning (lead white 3, yellow ochre 1.2, raw umber 1, red earth 0.35) -> came out lighter than expected: value 183, rgb 206,179,140.

  Design:
  - One-point perspective, eye level ~y 400, VP near door x~650. Back-wall floor line y~560.
  - Doorway (backlit, blazing pale outside light) at x ~590-790, y ~225-560: the biggest light. Batwing doors mid-height, swung inward by the zombie.
  - Zombie silhouetted in the doorway, lurching, one arm reaching; rim-lit edges; a burst of dark spatter off its shoulder against the light (the hit).
  - Light spill on the floor from the door toward us, the zombie's long shadow in it reaching toward the cowboy.
  - Cowboy lower-left foreground, crouched behind an overturned round card table (table to his right, tabletop facing the door), arm over the table, revolver flash ~ (540,400): the brightest small accent.
  - Hanging oil lamp upper left-center: warm halo, lights cowboy's hat/shoulders and table from above.
  - Bar along the right wall: dark mass, bottles with glints, a mirror catching door light.
  - Foreground floor: broken bottle, spilled cards and chips, glass shards glinting.
  - Gunsmoke drifting across, glowing in the door light: thin scumbles over dry paint.
  Value hierarchy: doorway > muzzle flash (small, most intense) > lamp > floor spill > smoke. Rest dark warm browns, cooler in the deepest shadows.
  Process: drawing (thin umber), lean dark lay-in (turps), dry; body; smoke scumbles; details; glazes.
- day 1, 13:55: ## Day 1 lay-in (09:00-14:00)
  - Drawing: thin round (w3, point 0.7) with raw umber+burnt sienna turps 0.5. b:stroke through corner points SMOOTHS them (rectangles came out rounded) - draw straight segments as separate strokes.
  - Scratch swatches over the tan ground: broad hand coverage 1.5 without fill leaves big gaps; body hand + fill=true, coverage 2, clip: solid. wallD (raw umber 2, bone black 1, burnt sienna 0.5, turps 0.3) laid with fill -> value ~62 (gallery ~74). warmD (umber 2, b.sienna 1.2, black 0.4) -> ~73, redder. turps 0.3 vs 0.15 made no visible difference in value.
  - Walls: broad hand with graded piles (glowW near the lamp, wallD, deepD in corners), fill, clipped. Strokes stay visible as horizontal streaks.
  - Door light: body hand, filbert 10 lay 2.5, piles sky/facade/street graded by y; three near-white creams (lead white + Naples yellow, + lemon chrome / umber+ultramarine / yellow ochre).
  - First zombie silhouette read as a boy waving. Lifted it with dipped rags (rag width 30, dip 0.95, pressure 0.85, 4 fresh rags, crossing angles): mostly lifted; residue at the mask edges (mask wipes stop inside). First rag filled at once (load 0.97) - use fresh rags.
  - Second zombie: both arms reaching left, hunched; left batwing leaf now fully open (an edge-on sliver at the jamb), right leaf curved top. Painted with zombD2 (bone black 1, raw umber 1.2, green earth 1.2) with detail round 4 into wet door light: reads as a lurching figure at full view, but the head is a big round blob (reads childlike) - reshape later with light over the set dark.
  - Lamp at (365,170-235): shade, chimney glow, flame, brass font. Crisp, cartoonish; needs halo and softening.
  - Bar (right) laid with deepD: too cool/blue. Warm it in body stage.
- day 12, 21:15: ## Day 3-12: body campaign 1
  - Back wall: body hand filbert 12, graded piles wallHi/wallMid/wallDk by a lamp-light function (lamp at 365,235, shade cuts light above y~150). Then after 9 days dry: glaze pile glazeDk (bone black 1, raw umber 1, burnt sienna 0.5, medium 0.3) hand=glaze over the room outside the lamp pool. Scratch trial first: on dry wallHi swatch one glaze pass of that pile took value 136 -> 98 (gallery), two passes -> 86. medium 0.6-0.75 glazes were too weak to deepen (barely visible). Blending the ring where the glaze stopped (badger, 2 passes crossing) softened the edge acceptably but left a visible oval of light.
  - Cowboy hat: first two hat attempts (wallHi on the crown, lit from lamp) came out as a bright yellow "plastic" ochre. Lifted with dipped rags (16 wide, dip 0.95, pressure 0.85-0.9, 2-3 fresh rags) - came off well because still open. Third: dark warm base (warmD/deepD) + a few gestures of wallMid then wallHi on the crown's lamp side. Better.
  - Cowboy: vest (bone black/umber/sienna), Indian-red sleeves, blue-gray trousers (bone black, ultramarine, umber, white), dark boots. Flat & doll-like still; needs modeling and rim light.
  - Table: overturned round top seen from its underside, planks vertical (flat 8, woodP), plank joints rigger deepD, a dark rim crescent on the right.
  - Bar front: barWood + deepD, stiles flat 4; blended, which softened stiles into streaks (fine). Brass foot rail: scrape with knife failed to remove the first stroke fully, so two rails show.
  - Palette: 16 piles max - scrape as you go. Wet paint needed 8+ days for the thick white door to set (lead white thick stays open long).
- day 16, 00:01: - LESSON: piles made with `local` (or mix{} into a local) can't be scraped later - palette{scrape=} wants the pile object, not its name. Two "zshadow" heaps are stuck on the board for good (14 usable slots now). Always keep piles global.
- day 29, 02:58: ## Day 12-29: redesign of the cowboy, table, lamp, door details
  - Critique of myself at day 15: the first cowboy was a stiff mannequin; arm straight out like a tube. Redrew: hunched torso, near arm bent forward to grip the table rim, gun arm extended over the table, revolver now ~ (460-532, 397-410). Old silhouette remnants painted out with wall colors in "halo" passes (detail filbert 5-6, coverage 3, fill, clipped), graded with the same lamp-light function as the wall so they match.
  - Halo repaint left of x=200 (left wall) came out slightly greener and lighter (gallery 78 vs 69 around) - fix with a warm dark glaze once dry.
  - Table face redone: planks running horizontally toward a VP far right (1500,400), two battens, joints rigger. Reads as the underside of a round table now.
  - Lamp redone smaller: dark tin shade (top), glowing underside ellipse, glass chimney with lampGlow+sky, flame stroke (round 4 point 0.7 lay 4, sky pile), brass font.
  - Zombie head: carved with sky paint (detail round 2.5 lay 2 over dry silhouette) - gaping jaw, brow, nose; hair strands with rigger. Thin rigger hair strands sprang out like antennae - lifted with a rag (width 8, dip 0.95) while open; good.
  - Louvers on right batwing: round 1.8 lines of mix(sky, wallHi) clipped to the panel. Reads as louvers.
  - Zombie's shadow on the floor spill: first try was a wrong direction/too small; second clipped to spillM. The spill also crossed the table base (lifted with rag, repainted wood).
  Values now: doorway 228, lamp wall ~150, floor spill ~140, table face 78, trousers 78, sleeves 72, face 90, vest ~58.
- day 37, 04:09: ## Day 37: critic's visit (mid-painting) - plan
  Critic: (1) cowboy is lit by no light in the room: glaze him down a step, light only top planes (lamp, warm) and front edges (door, pale rim). (2) Gun arm comes out of his throat (scarf same red as sleeve) - change scarf to dull ochre/dirty white with knot; arm emerges from behind the chest; head must tilt down/forward, chin tucked, looking along barrel; light bar under brim reads as bandage; arm is a tube - taper, elbow fold, cuff; hand is a ball - make a fist with thumb, grip into hand, finger at guard; kneeling leg = flipper boot: shin trouser color, boot heel up, toe digging; stray pale stroke on trousers. (3) Spill same value as door - glaze down a step, crisp at threshold softening toward us, lintel edge softest. Lamp pool evenly bright with hard ragged edge - make falloff rings by glazing, darken wall above the shade, chimney/flame must step above. (4) Zombie shadow wrong slant: should be parallel to the spill's right edge (~45 deg), leave both feet, head ~(565,650), arms branching left to (510-530, 625-640); crisp at feet, softer toward head; scrape floor-light slivers at (300-320,680-690),(370-390,655-680). (5) Zombie back merges with leaf edge - sliver of light between; table crossbar lines up with chair rail - tilt; table needs lit edge on right; flash against the dark between barrel tip and jamb (535-585); smoke thickest near the door, thin over the cowboy.
  Order: A redraw upper cowboy -> B lamp pool rings + cowboy glaze/relight -> C spill/shadow -> E small fixes -> F smoke, flash, details.
- day 47, 09:50: ## Day 37-47: acting on the critique
  - Head/hat redrawn with outline{} masks (hat3c crown, hat3b brim, head3 -> face4 profile with brow, nose tip, lips, chin), head lower and forward, chin over the bandana. Painted dark (skinSh/warmD/hatDk) with light only from the lamp on the crown's right side and the brim's front edge, and door light (skinLit + rim) on the profile. Blended the face lightly (badger, shrunk mask) - good soft modeling. An earlier head attempt at a bright crown/peach face was lifted with rags while open (works well: 4 rags, dip 0.95, pressure 0.9).
  - Gun arm tapered (armR2 ribbon 26->16), sleeveDk with a warm underside, elbow fold, cuff, sleeveLit top. Fist (fist4 outline) with thumb, knuckle row, trigger finger + guard, grip butt.
  - Kneeling leg: shin lying on floor (shin5), boot standing on toe with heel up (boot5/heel5), contact shadow blended.
  - Spill: lifted the first repaint with 6 dipped rags (width 30). Repainted inside a hard parallel-sided mask (left edge x=590-2.254(y-560), right x=790-(y-560); both converge at (949,400) on the horizon = the sun's vanishing point on the floor). Grade floorLit at threshold -> spillLo further out; band of floorSh painted wet just outside; blended a band whose width grows 1.5->15 toward us: right edge reads as a proper penumbra. Bottom (lintel) edge: blend smeared light down; repainted strip with floorSh and one vertical blend; still ~78 vs 69 around - needs a dark glaze once dry.
  - Zombie shadow geometry (computed with inverse-depth): feet ~ (695,562) -> hip shadow (660,584) -> shoulders (596,625) -> head top (566,644); line x = 695 - 1.568(y-562). Arms run nearly level left from the shoulders into the table at x~530.
  - Spill value now 193 near threshold, 177 out; door 228. Plan a warm glaze (burnt sienna 1, raw umber 0.6, medium 0.5: on scratch 196 -> 163) graded toward the viewer.
- day 77, 15:14: ## Day 47-77
  - Lamp pool repainted as a falloff (lampLit2: 1/(1+(d/125)^2) times a cone cut by the shade; graded wallHi/wallMid/warmD/wallDk by "hat" weights) with body filbert 8 coverage 2.5 + two crossing blends; then an outer strip and seam blend, then glazeDk over the dim part. Now reads as light falling off from the lamp with a dark ceiling above the shade. Good.
  - Glaze 'work(..., coverage=function)' is not allowed (coverage must be a number).
  - Spill warm glaze: gWarm (burnt sienna 1, raw umber 0.6, medium 0.75) once over all, again over y>600; dry-rag partial lift near threshold. Spill now ~165-185 vs door 225. Lintel edge: blend left a smear; a glaze + rag lift + a blended dark notch fixed it partly.
  - Zombie shadow repainted along the sun direction (VP 949,400): legs from both feet, torso, head ~ (532,633), two arms reaching left to x~440 on the spill. Reads as cast by him now.
  - Near arm redrawn (upperL/foreL ribbons, handL fist gripping the table rim), table leg moved to slope down-left (leg1N) so it no longer lines up with the chair rail. Lit rim along the table's door-side edge (wallHi top, rim pile lower).
  - Glazed trousers, near arm, bandana and the shadow side of the face with glazeDk once: the cowboy now sits darker against the lamp pool.
  - SMOKE TRIALS (scratch, over dry wallDk ~ value 60, 14 days):
    * glaze hand with a mask: the film is uniform inside the mask (soft/noisy masks do NOT modulate it) -> hard-edged "cigar"; puff-ellipse unions read as cotton beads. Rejected.
    * badger strokes, light load (0.25), pressure 0.15-0.35: streaky drift, hair-like. Maybe for wisps.
    * WORKS: stipple(area, {pile=smokeW2 (lead white 3, yellow ochre 1.2, Naples 0.5, burnt sienna 0.15, medium 0.85), width=10, coverage=function = 2.5*density, feather=1, pressure {0.2,0.5}, dips {30,0.4,0}}) where density = plume envelope * billow noise; then blend(area:grow(8):blur(8)) along the drift, and a second blend crossing (angle 0.6). Soft, irregular, dissolving edges. Thin white over dark reads cool-gray -> keep it warm (ochre) except in the door light.
- day 83, 23:57: ## Day 77-83 + flash/smoke trials
  - Shelves + 21 bottles on the right wall (glassG viridian/black, glassA sienna/black), glints with rim pile. Read as a back bar.
  - Barrel re-aimed upward: ribbon (478,401)->(529,385), tip at (530,385), direction -0.30 rad (aim line hits the zombie's chest/shoulder ~ (680,340)).
  - Bottom floor band: a series of failures. Strip repainted with body hand then blended -> horizontal smudged band with a hard rectangle edge. LESSON: blend over a rect mask on a floor of oriented boards leaves a hard-edged smeared rectangle; edge="soft" on a body pass gives a ragged comb edge. What finally worked: 8 fresh dipped rags to lift everything open, then repaint the whole bottom (rect blurred 5, edge soft, full canvas width so no side edges), graded piles, then 3 blends crossing (0, 1.3, 0) over a blurred rect. Result: a soft warm-dark foreground, lintel edge of the spill soft. Still a slightly smudged band (y 670-750) - acceptable as the dim foreground; later: rebuild board lines + cards/bottle there.
  - Flash trials (scratch, over dry wallDk): flash4 = 9 sharp tongues (round point 0.95, flashR = orange chrome 1, vermilion 0.6, cad yellow 0.3), 6 orange (flashO), 3 yellow (flashY), core stroke + touch (flashCore lead white 4 + lemon chrome 1, lay 9). Reads as a burst. Glow: thin yellowish piles over dark go OLIVE/greenish; best glow pile = glowP: cadmium red 0.4, orange chrome 1, lead white 0.5, cadmium yellow 0.3, stippled (width 7, coverage 3*hot^2, feather 1) then two crossing blends.
  - Smoke over dark reads cool gray whatever the warm tint (thin light over dark). Accept: gunsmoke is gray; in door light use smokeLit (lead white 3, Naples 0.8, ochre 0.6, medium 0.85).
  - UNEXPLAINED: one stippled+blended glow (orange chrome 1, Naples 0.5, vermilion 0.3, lead white 0.8, no medium) came out pure black 0,0,0 and 'setting' on the scratch; repeating the same recipe elsewhere did not reproduce it. Probe after any new mixed passage.
- day 105, 02:14: ## Day 83-105
  - Foreground: board joints restated (rigger, jointP) incl. 8 more to the left; 5 cards (quads foreshortened 0.42-0.5) + pips; broken bottle (first try on the dark foreground read as a cartoon; lifted). Second bottle placed in the spill near (652,636) lying on its side: glassA body, amber transmitted glow (orange chrome/raw sienna/Naples), rim highlight, broken neck apart, cast shadow toward viewer, spilled whiskey pool with a door reflection. Pool first came out dark (puddleP over the lit floor) -> lifted & refilled with a pale glare pile. Reads.
  - Gunsmoke: stipple smokeG (lead white 3, Naples 0.8, ochre 0.6, medium 0.85) with density = cone envelope along the barrel (rot -0.42) * billow noise, protected the figure; 3 blends. Over dark wall it is gray; reads as smoke.
  - Flash: glow stipple glowP (cad red 0.4, orange chrome 1, white 0.5, cad yellow 0.3) cov 3*hot^2 + 2 blends; then flash4 at (533,383) scale 0.75 rot -0.30: 9 red tongues, 6 orange, 3 yellow, core = sky pile lay 9. Reads as a burst against the dark jamb.
  - Hit: gore spatter (bone black/umber/Indian red, medium 0.45) round 5 load 0.9 force 0.25-0.4 toward up-right, clipped to the door minus the zombie: 300 droplets on the bright doorway behind his shoulder + 4 tapered strokes. Low force = bigger drops. Reads as the hit.
  - Haze in the door-light shaft: stipple smokeLit2 cov 2*den, den = triangle from door's left jamb to spill corner * billow noise; blended along 2.12 rad. Subtle.
  - Face: repainting the face base then blending everything erased the features (blend over a whole open passage flattens it). Waited 5 days for the base to dry, then laid features as soft low-pressure gestures over dry paint: brim shadow band, eye socket, lit cheek (skinMid), ear, mustache, stubble, flashLit profile edge (Naples 1, orange chrome 0.5, white 0.5, red earth 0.2). Readable at full view, still a bit cartoonish up close.

Second visit (day 105). Since your last notes: cowboy head redrawn lower and forward (profile, brim shadow, door/flash light on the profile), bandana now ochre, gun arm tapered with cuff and fold, fist with thumb and trigger finger, near arm now grips the table rim, kneeling leg redrawn (shin on the floor, boot on its toe), lamp pool repainted as a falloff with a dark ceiling above the shade, spill glazed down and its edges graded (crisp at threshold, soft toward us), zombie shadow re-angled along the sun's direction from both feet, sliver of light between zombie's back and the batwing, table leg re-angled off the chair rail, table door-side rim lit. New: muzzle flash against the dark jamb, gunsmoke, haze in the door shaft, hit spatter behind the zombie's shoulder, bottles on the back bar, cards/bottle/whiskey pool on the floor. What would you still fix, most important first? I'm especially unsure about the cowboy's torso (a big flat dark mass), the face up close, and whether the smoke reads.

content.thinking:
Looking more closely, the cowboy's pose reads as lunging rather than crouching, with his near arm punching toward the table rim and his gun arm extending over it. He's actually positioned beside the table rather than behind it, standing to its left with little real cover.

The leg extending left into a boot reads as a lunging stride, his torso is a flat dark vest shape, and his face has a cartoonish, caricature quality. The zombie is a rope-armed silhouette reaching toward the door jamb with white wispy hair, and the table itself looks more like an oval barrel lid or shield than a true table — its shadow falls toward the lower left, reaching the table's base.

I'm checking whether the hazy smudge near the door jamb actually reads as smoke or just a dirty wall mark, confirming the lamp halo and rays, the muzzle flash, and the spatter particles behind the zombie's shoulder read correctly. I'm also verifying the bar and bottles on the right wall, the dark back wall between the lamp pool and door, and making sure the light logic holds — the floor spill and zombie shadow both trail toward the lower left, consistent with backlight spilling in from outside the door. The gun's muzzle flash aim line also correctly lines up with the zombie's chest.

content.thinking:
Only one squinted image came back, showing the doorway dominating with the zombie readable, while the cowboy and table merge into one dark mass against the lamp's light pool. That lamp pool reads oddly as a V-shaped fan with two lobes going up-left and up-right, like horns, which seems off since the shade should contain the light differently.

I'm trying to reconcile this: those bright lobes rise above the lamp level on the back wall, which only makes physical sense if light from the flame is slipping past the edges of the flat shade and fanning upward and outward onto the wall behind it.

That shadow pattern would produce a dark wedge directly above the shade with brighter light to either side, which could plausibly account for those odd "cat ear" shapes rather than them being actual rays or horns. I want to zoom in further and also check the zombie, door, and smoke details to confirm.

content.thinking:
I'm noticing the lamp's shade reads as a dark disk with a bright underside, and the wall behind it forms a lit wedge with a notch above it, while an ochre glow outlines the shade, chimney, and base like a sticker effect, giving the whole thing a crisp, cartoonish look.

A bigger problem is that the hat's brim should catch strong warm light since its top plane faces directly up toward the lamp, but instead it's rendered flat and dark — that's a clear miss unless the lamp sits further back near the wall rather than directly above the cowboy, in which case the light falloff would make sense.

Looking at the figure overall: the face is lit from the front, but the hat, vest, and torso are rendered as flat dark shapes with little top-plane lighting, which contradicts the earlier critique about lighting only the upper surfaces. I'm also trying to work out the arm positions — since he faces right, the viewer sees his left side, so the gun arm reaching across the table appears to be the far (right) arm emerging from behind the chest, while the near (left) arm runs down from the shoulder to a fist resting on the table rim.

I'm now tracing the lower body: the oversized, flat torso narrows into a hip, from which one trouser leg extends down toward a boot on one side and the other leg bends toward the knee and boot on the opposite side, though it's tricky to tell exactly which leg goes where in the composition.

There's also a lighter diagonal smear across the thigh area — a pale gray streaky band that could be a stray glare or reflective highlight — plus a small round grayish blob nearby that might be an incidental mark or small object.

Looking at the overturned table, it reads as a tall narrow ellipse with planks and a dark rim, more like a barrel or oval tub-shield than a round tabletop — the proportions suggest we're seeing its underside at an angle, standing upright facing the door to shield the cowboy from the zombie.

I notice a diagonal gray band crossing the cowboy's thigh that could be a table leg, but it reads more like a ghostly translucent smear with a faint highlight sliver near its lower edge, which is confusing given where it sits relative to the table's underside.

The near arm's fist rests at the table's upper left edge, almost like it's gripping the rim or punching toward it, with a diagonal crossbar running from the fist toward the upper right. The far arm extends in that same dull red tube-like color down to a fist holding a small dark gun with knuckle lines visible.

The gun itself is odd — the barrel looks far too thin and long relative to the tiny frame, more like a wand with a flash at its tip than an actual revolver. Then I shift to the face: a profile with a closed eye reading as sleeping or smug, a large highlighted nose, mustache, and salmon-pink shading on the cheek.

That lighter band under the brim still reads ambiguously as a headband rather than brim shadow. For the zombie, the silhouette is dark and mottled with rope-like lumpy arms and a few stray hair strands at the back of the head, plus a spatter trailing up-right from the shoulder suggesting an impact.

The zombie's arms reach toward the left jamb — possibly grabbing the door frame or reaching toward the cowboy — while its legs carry the body walking leftward, which stays consistent. The doorway itself is a flat near-white rectangle with a faint pale smudge suggesting an exterior horizon, but otherwise featureless, which works fine for the blazing light effect, though the hard rectangular upper edge of the door stands out.

Looking again at the table's surface, the thick dark oval rim combined with vertical battens and horizontal plank lines makes it ambiguous — it could read as a barrel top, an oval wooden door, or a round table tipped on its side.

If I treat it as a tipped table viewed at an angle, the long axis of the ellipse would run vertical, with the rim's thickness showing as a crescent shading on one edge and the legs projecting toward the viewer to sell the "table" read. Since the tabletop surface likely faces the door while the underside faces the cowboy, the legs would need to project from that underside toward him — which explains the pale diagonal shape crossing his thigh as a table leg, though right now it's rendered too translucent and ghostly to read as solid wood; I want to crop in and check that leg more carefully.

content.text:
**Second visit, day 105**

The picture reads now. The door and zombie hold the strongest place. The spill and the shadow cast from both feet are convincing, and the bottle and whiskey pool earn their spot. The lamp's falloff is right: the dark wedge above the shade with light rising on either side is what a disc shade throws onto a wall behind it. The cowboy finally sits in the lamp pool as a dark shape. Here is what I'd still fix, in order.

**1. Start with the jamb strip and the smoke (x 520–610, y 250–650).**
You asked whether the smoke reads. It doesn't. It reads as a gray stain or bare plaster on the wall. There are four reasons:
- **Its shape.** It's a vertical slab running from about y 250 down to the floor, not a cloud. Its right edge is cut hard by the jamb.
- **Its value.** In value view it's almost the same as the wall. It separates from the wall by hue (cool gray on warm brown), not by light, and that's how a stain separates.
- **No source.** It isn't densest or brightest at the muzzle, so nothing ties it to the gun.
- **It stops at the door,** which is exactly where smoke would be most visible.

This strip is also where the whole picture hinges. The flash, the zombie's fingers and the jamb edge all meet within about 60 units. The fingers stop exactly on the jamb edge, a tangency that glues them to the frame and flattens the distance between a foreground man and a figure several metres back.

What I'd do:
- **Calm the column.** Glaze its lower part (y 450–650) back toward the wall with gWarm or glazeDk, so it stops being a column.
- **Restipple a real cloud from the muzzle at (530,385).** Make it densest there and warm with the flash (your glowP family), drifting up-right along the aim and rolling upward. Over the dark wall it needs to be a clear step lighter than the wall, around 100–110 near the muzzle, not just grayer.
- **Carry it across the jamb.** Let it cover the door's left 30–50 units and partly veil the zombie's hands. Over the cream, don't use white; it would disappear. Use a thin, slightly darker warm gray, around 200 against the door's 228. A thin dark veil over light turns warm amber, which is what backlit smoke looks like, so the optics are on your side here.

That one move makes the smoke read, softens the hard jamb edge, buries the finger tangency, and puts air between the two figures.

While you're there, look at the zombie's arms. Their lighter mottled texture reads as knotted rope or chain. Bring them to the body's dark, smooth, with only their edges slightly eaten by the light. If any fingertip stays clear of the smoke, leave a sliver of light between it and the jamb, like the gap you left behind his back.

**2. The torso.**
You're right that it's a flat dark mass. The darkness is fine, because he is backlit. What's missing is structure and edges. Right now it's a bean: too deep from chest to back, bulging to about x 180, upright, with no waist.

Keep the mass dark and add:
- **The vest's front edge,** from under the bandana knot (about 285,420) to the hip (about 300,550), with a narrow strip of darkened shirt red showing. This also explains where the gun arm comes from: out of the shirt, not the throat area.
- **A gunbelt across the hips** (y about 540–555), dipping toward the front, with a holster on the near hip. The pale gray blob at (290,540) either becomes the buckle catching the flash or gets painted out.
- **Two thin lights.** A warm lamp-lit band along the top of the hunched back and near shoulder (190–240, 398–415), kept in your wallMid range, not the plastic yellow. A pale door rim down the chest's front edge under the gun arm.
- **Flash light on the gun forearm.** It's right next to the flash, so its front half should glow orange and fade toward the elbow. At the moment it's uniform dull red.
- If you're willing, take the back in by 20–30 units with your halo passes so it becomes one hunched curve from nape to hip.

The near upper arm also reads as a suspender strap. Give the shoulder a deltoid curve and the elbow a turn.

**3. The table leg crossing his thigh (about 290–370, 520–645).**
It's translucent, so it reads as a pane of glass or a smear on the trousers. Either commit to it or remove it:
- **Commit:** make it opaque wood, with a lamp-lit upper edge, a dark cast shadow on the trouser beneath it, and a turned foot at the end. Lose the little gray cylinder at its top.
- **Remove:** paint the trouser back.

Half-transparent is the worst of both.

**4. The face.**
At full view the expression reads as dozing and content, which undercuts the shot. Up close, the trouble is specific:
- **The eye.** A closed line reads as asleep. Drop the brow into a hard angle over a dark socket with a narrow slit. One tiny warm glint from the flash would say "aiming".
- **The pink bars** on the mid-cheek and lower lip read as blush, and in gallery view as a grin. Light from the door and flash should follow the profile: a narrow band down the brow ridge, nose, mustache and chin, widest on the cheekbone just behind the nose. Glaze the mid-cheek bar to a half-tone. Make the mouth a firm closed line.
- **The light band under the brim** still reads as a headband. It's the brim's shadow, so it should be darker than the face, not lighter.
- **Gallery light:** the ridges of the hair strokes behind the face catch light and flash gray, so he reads as white-haired. Knock the ridges down with the knife.

**5. The revolver reads as a wand.**
It's a thin line with one highlight running its full length. Add:
- a cylinder bulge just ahead of the fist
- a cocked hammer spur above the thumb
- a front sight at the tip
- a highlight broken up and brightest near the muzzle

**6. Small things:**
- **The lamp's ochre outlines** ring the shade, chimney and font like a sticker. The top of the shade faces away from the flame and shouldn't glow. Keep the glow around the chimney and under the shade only.
- **The bright diagonal line at bottom right** (830,580 to 995,745) escorts the eye straight out of the corner. Dim it toward the corner.

Start with 1. It's mostly scumbling over dry paint with a stipple method you already trust, and it repairs the one place where two figures, the flash and the story all meet. Then do 2, since the torso is the largest unresolved area on the protagonist.
